title: Critical Microsoft Entra ID RCE Flaw Allows Remote Attackers to Execute Code
content_md: Microsoft has disclosed a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability affecting Microsoft Entra ID, tracked as CVE-2026-69836. The flaw, released on August 20, 2026, stemmed from deserialization of untrusted data and could allow an unauthorized attacker to execute code remotely over a network. Customers do not need to install patches, change configurations, or take other remediation steps, according to Microsoft’s advisory. CVE-2026-69836 carries a Critical severity rating and is classified under CWE-502, Deserialization of Untrusted Data. Critical Microsoft Entra ID RCE Flaw This weakness occurs when an application accepts serialized data from an untrusted source and reconstructs it without adequate validation or safeguards. In cloud identity infrastructure, unsafe deserialization can be particularly dangerous. A successful exploit could enable an attacker to manipulate application processing and execute attacker-controlled code in the vulnerable service’s context. Microsoft’s advisory describes the impact as remote code execution, indicating that exploitation could occur across a network without requiring physical access to affected infrastructure. The company has not released detailed technical exploitation information, proof-of-concept code, attack prerequisites, or specific affected service components.
